checks.title: Audit hash chain is intact
checks.limitation: A local hash chain detects edits and mid-file deletion, not truncation of the newest events or a full rewrite by someone with write access.

checks.title: Requirement content hashes match their recorded fields
Current-revision evidence files still match their recorded SHA-256
checks.limitation: A hash match proves the file is unchanged since linking; it does not prove the file demonstrates the requirement.

checks.title: No false completion: every attested requirement has current approval, code, passed test-run and release evidence
Approvals and attestations are bound to a valid revision
Imported test and release claims keep their "not independently verified" label
checks.note: No imported claim has been upgraded

checks.title: Approvals never claim a verified identity
Registry state is explained by the audit log (no silent edits)
checks.note: Every approval, link, attestation and revision has a matching audit event
checks.limitation: Consistency is checked by counts per requirement, not by cryptographic binding of each registry field.

checks.title: Source files are classified untrusted and hash-pinned
checks.note: All sources carry untrusted-input label and SHA-256

checks.title: Stale evidence is visible, not silently reused
checks.note: 3 stale link(s) preserved as history across 1 requirement(s)

limitations: Local reviewer identity is self-attested; there is no SSO or signature.
Imported test-run and release outcomes are user-supplied claims; this tool never executes tests.
The audit chain is tamper-evident for edits, not tamper-proof against a full rewrite.
Secret redaction is heuristic. A PASS verdict is not a certification, legal opinion or proof that software is correct.
